## Summary

**What I found.** I opened the renders and both reference photos, then audited the gear numerically against the source. The layout was never the bug — measured against the real 747 ACAP figures, the track, wheel diameter, and ride height are all already correct, which is why iter 11's "+30% rescale" and iter 16's full rebuild each bought nothing. The gear fails on two things, and both are arithmetic you can read straight off the source.

**A race, first.** Between my Read and my Edit, a concurrent actor running my same prompt wrote an "Iter 19" into the file (1029 → 1139 lines). This is the exact collision that got iter 6 rejected, so I stopped and re-read instead of forcing my write. Iter 19 had independently found one of my two root causes — `makeOleo` painted `CHROME` (near-white) at local y=0 and dark at y=len, i.e. the leg was near-white exactly where it hangs in free air and dark only where it's buried in the hull, so to a camera there were no legs at all — and fixed it, plus opened the *fore/aft* tyre gap (`TRUCK_HALF` 0.8 → 0.92) and braced the wing legs. **I left all of that alone.** Re-applying it would have collided and double-fixed the same thing.

**What I fixed: the axis iter 19 didn't measure.** A 747 truck has four tyres separated on *two* axes — two axles apart in x (iter 19 opened that), and two **duals** apart in z. The duals sit at ±0.55 with half-width 0.26, so their inner faces are at ±0.29 and the channel between them is 0.58 wide. The beam meant to run *down* that channel was built at `halfW 0.32` — **wider than the gap.** It didn't part the duals, it plugged them, overlapping each tyre by 0.03. Beam (`0x3a4048`) and tyre (`0x14171b`) are the same near-black, so every truck fused into one solid slab. That's the half of Claude's "more clearly separated **wheel pairs**" still standing: a wheel pair *is* the dual pair, it's separated along z, and no colour law or fore/aft
